title: Brains and machines: neural networks as models of the brain
stage: Graduate study and research in neuroscience
audience: a graduate preparing for research in neuroscience or cognitive science, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Study the two-way exchange between neuroscience and artificial intelligence at graduate level: the history from perceptrons to deep learning, deep networks as models of the visual system, comparing models and brains with encoding models and representational similarity analysis, recurrent networks as models of cognition and dynamics, reinforcement learning and the dopamine system, learning rules and the question of backpropagation in the brain, predictive coding, language models and the brain's language network, and what such comparisons can and cannot show.
primary_reading: Neuromatch Academy computational neuroscience course materials (free online)

weeks.1: From perceptrons to deep learning: the shared history
weeks.2: Deep networks as models of the ventral visual stream
weeks.5: Recurrent networks as models of cognition
weeks.8: Learning rules: is there backpropagation in the brain?
weeks.10: Language models and the brain's language network
weeks.11: What model–brain comparisons can and cannot show

blocks.deliverable: Compare layers of a toy network with supplied neural responses.
Compute and compare representational dissimilarity matrices in code.
Train a tiny recurrent network on a timing task.
Week 7 midterm; compare a biologically plausible rule with gradient descent on a toy task.
Evaluate a claim that a language model predicts brain activity.
Write a referee-style critique of a model–brain paper.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Model–brain comparison: compare the internal representations of a small network you train on your own computer with a supplied set of neural or behavioral responses, using an encoding model and representational similarity analysis with proper cross-validation and noise ceilings, and write a workshop-style paper that states what the comparison shows and the strongest alternative explanation.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
